values.description: Both tiers are served by the same host; the credential selects the tier.
Your production API key. The SAME collection runs on either tier — swap this value, change nothing else.
Which tier this environment selects. Only the Telegram test scripts read it, to assert the documented 403 a sandbox credential receives; no request branches on it.

The address to inspect. Any address valid on {{sample_network}}. In the sandbox this is the documented FIXTURE input, so POST /api/v1/check returns the deterministic fixture report rather than a simulated one.
Network slug. See integration/capability-matrix.md for the supported set.

An ERC-20 CONTRACT address, for the token operations. A wallet address is not a token and will not analyze as one. The production default is USDC on Ethereum; the sandbox answers from a fixture whatever contract you pass.
A block height for the block/MEV operations. The sandbox answers from a deterministic fixture whatever height you pass.
An ANALYSIS report id, from POST /api/v1/check. Consumed by the async status poll and by GET /api/reports/{id}. The test script captures it for you.
The INTEGER analysis id from POST /api/v1/multichain/analyze's 202. Consumed only by the progress poll. Not a report id, and not a UUID.
The SAVED multi-chain report's public UUID. POST /api/v1/multichain/scan auto-saves and returns it; the saved-report resolve and GET both take it.

A saved BLOCK/MEV report id, captured by POST /api/v1/block/analyze — which saves the report and returns its public id. The resolve and fetch below take that UUID; blockNumber + network correlation remains supported but is not the preferred path.

An AI investigation id, captured by GET /api/investigations. Not by the create: POST /api/investigate answers a server-sent event stream, which a Postman script cannot reliably read, so the list immediately after it is the producer.
A watchlist ENTRY id, captured by POST /api/watchlist. The update, delete and per-item alert requests consume it.
A custom LABEL id, captured by POST /api/labels.

A share token, which the owner of the report generates and gives you. The two share operations take NO credential: the share token IS the credential, so treat it as a secret and never commit a real one — anyone holding it can read that report.
